description: A model used in narrative fiction that divides a story into three parts (acts), often called the Setup, the Confrontation, and the Resolution.

climax.description: The scene or sequence in which the main tensions of the story are brought to their most intense point and the dramatic question is answered.

confrontation.description: The second act, also referred to as rising action: the protagonist's attempt to resolve the problem.

dramaticQuestion.description: The dramatic question, framed in terms of the protagonist's call to action.

firstPlotPoint.description: Signals the end of the first act and raises a dramatic question that will be answered in the climax.

incitingIncident.description: A dynamic, on-screen incident, the inciting incident or catalyst, that confronts the protagonist.

resolution.description: The third act features the resolution of the story and its subplots.

setup.description: The first act establishes the main characters, their relationships, and the world they live in.

title: Three-act structure
